Felony = can carry up to 3 years in jail. 1:16 Felony = can carry up to 3 years in jail. 1:16 Sync to video time Description Penal Code 236 PC & 237 PC: The crime of "false imprisonment" 74Likes5,688Views2019Feb 21 Per Penal Code 236 and 237, "false imprisonment" is defined as “the unlawful violation of the personal liberty of another." This occurs when one person restrains, detains, or confines another person without his/her consent. The crime can be committed with or without force or violence. Under Penal Code 236 PC and 237 PC, false imprisonment is a wobbler, meaning the prosecutor could file the charge as either a misdemeanor or a felony. It carries a penalty of up to 3 years in state prison. But as the California criminal defense lawyer explains in this video, cases are rarely clear cut. It is often possible to fight the case successfully, getting the charges reduced or dismissed.
